features.t: Buckets (insert, list, get, patch/update, delete)
x: Bucket create/patch/delete complete synchronously in Vyomi; the real API can return a long-running operation for cross-location moves.

features.t: Objects (list, get, insert — simple/multipart/resumable — delete, compose, range downloads, folders)
Lifecycle rules (Delete / SetStorageClass actions)
x: Age, createdBefore, matchesPrefix/Suffix, matchesStorageClass and the custom-time conditions are evaluated against real object fields and really delete or transition objects (swept lazily on every request against the bucket's objects, not once a day like the real API).

features.t: Bucket IAM policy (getIamPolicy / setIamPolicy), uniform/fine-grained access control, public access prevention
x: Public access prevention is ENFORCED: setIamPolicy really rejects a binding that grants allUsers/allAuthenticatedUsers while the bucket's publicAccessPrevention is 'enforced'. Beyond that one write-time check, Vyomi has no per-request authorization layer — a policy set before PAP was enforced, or object ACLs under fine-grained access, never block an actual read/write.

features.t: Bucket retention policy
Object holds (temporaryHold / eventBasedHold) and per-object retention (Object Retention Lock)
x: A locked bucket retention policy can't be shortened or removed in real GCS; Vyomi enforces the retention window itself but does not separately model the isLocked governance step.

features.t: Batch Operations (bulk Delete / SetStorageClass jobs over a bucket+prefix)
x: Modeled as a sub-resource of Vyomi's own Cloud Storage wire (/storage/v1/batchOperations) rather than the real separate storagebatchoperations.googleapis.com service, since no google-cloud-storage client calls it directly.

features.t: Insights datasets (Storage Intelligence inventory/usage dataset configs)
x: Dataset configs are accepted and listed exactly like the real create/list calls, but Vyomi never runs the underlying export — no BigQuery dataset is populated.

features.t: Cross-origin resource sharing (CORS) configuration
x: ENFORCED for real: an OPTIONS preflight and a matching GET (object or bucket) now carry the configured Access-Control-Allow-Origin/Methods/Expose-Headers/Max-Age response headers when the request's Origin matches a cors rule, and carry none when it doesn't — same as the real API, which also leaves the actual cross-origin block to the browser rather than the server.

features.t: Static website configuration (main page suffix / 404 page)
x: ENFORCED for real: Vyomi serves the configured mainPageSuffix object (and notFoundPage on a miss, with a real 404 status) on its own simulated public host at /storage/website/{bucket}/ — never the real storage.googleapis.com website host or a custom domain, since nothing in Vyomi ever reaches the real internet.

features.t: Requester Pays billing
x: ENFORCED for real on object data-plane calls (list/get/insert/delete): once billing.requesterPays is on, a request without a userProject query parameter is rejected with the real UserProjectMissing 400 error, matching gsutil/google-cloud-storage's own behaviour.

features.t: Object versioning (noncurrent object versions)
x: ENFORCED for real: turning on bucket.versioning.enabled makes an overwrite or delete archive the prior generation instead of discarding it — ?versions=true lists every generation, a single object GET/download accepts ?generation=N for any of them, and a generation-targeted DELETE permanently removes just that one version.

features.t: Soft delete policy (for data recovery)
x: ENFORCED for real: a bucket with softDeletePolicy.retentionDurationSeconds set archives a deleted/overwritten object's prior generation, lists it under ?softDeleted=true, and restores it to a NEW current generation via objects.restore — exactly the real recovery flow.

features.t: Data encryption with customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK)
x: Setting a bucket's default Cloud KMS key validates the CryptoKey resource-name shape and really stamps that kmsKeyName onto every object written to the bucket afterward, and Vyomi checks the key exists in Cloud KMS and lives in the bucket's location (it does not check the key is enabled or that the bucket's service agent may use it); object bytes are still stored under Google-managed encryption underneath — no real envelope encryption with that key ever happens.

features.t: Hierarchical namespace (HNS buckets with true folders)
x: ENFORCED for real: a bucket created with hierarchicalNamespace.enabled (which requires uniform bucket-level access, same as the real API, and is immutable afterward) gets a real Folders sub-resource — create/get/list/delete, plus an atomic rename that moves every object and subfolder under the source folder in ONE operation.

features.t: Resource tags (GCP-wide tag bindings, distinct from labels)
x: ENFORCED for real against Resource Manager's own Tags v3 API (tagKeys/tagValues/tagBindings — core/gcp_resourcemanager_core.py): adding a tag auto-provisions the tagKey/tagValue if new, binds it to the bucket's full resource name, and real API constraints apply (at most one value per tag key bound to a resource).

features.t: Advisor security recommendations (bucket posture findings)
x: Recommendations come from a deterministic rule engine over the real stored buckets (public allUsers/allAuthenticatedUsers IAM bindings, uniform bucket-level access off, public access prevention not enforced, no versioning/retention, no CMEK). The bucket list 'Security insights' column shows the per-bucket count and top severity of the same findings plus Vyomi detector alerts. They are not IAM Recommender / Security Command Center output: no usage-pattern ML, no excess-permission analysis and no data-sensitivity scanning.

features.t: Monitoring (Cloud Monitoring charts: request/error rates, bandwidth)
x: ENFORCED for real: every request against a bucket records a real point on Cloud Monitoring's own storage.googleapis.com/api/request_count metric (resource type gcs_bucket) — derived from actual API activity, not synthetic data — readable through the normal timeSeries.list API and charted for real on the Monitoring page.

features.t: Anywhere Cache (create, pause, resume, disable, update TTL / admission policy)
x: The cache resource and its creating/running/paused/disabled lifecycle, zone-vs-bucket-location, one-cache-per-zone, TTL (1h-7d) and admission-policy validation are real and stateful.

features.t: Long-running bucket operations (rename/relocate bucket, Turbo replication switch)
x: The Turbo replication switch now records a real, listable /b/{bucket}/operations resource. Every operation Vyomi records is already DONE at creation, though — bucket operations complete synchronously (see gcp.storage.buckets), so there is no RUNNING state to poll, and bucket rename/relocate is not modeled.

features.t: Inventory reports (Storage Insights report configs + generated CSV reports in a destination bucket)
x: Report configs (storageinsights v1 reportConfigs) are validated for real and the report is a REAL CSV of the source bucket's objects (+ manifest) written to the destination bucket, listable via reportDetails.

features.t: Project access settings (public access prevention for the project, Cloud Storage service account, Cloud Storage IDs)
Object enrichments (Smart Storage — Document AI classification/extraction on upload)
x: Enrichments run Document AI (and other Vertex AI pipelines) against newly uploaded objects; Vyomi has no ML inference engine to classify or extract from object content.

features.t: Interoperable access (HMAC keys for service/user accounts)
x: HMAC key issuance, listing, the ACTIVE/INACTIVE state toggle and delete-when-INACTIVE round-trip for real under projects/{project}/hmacKeys, but Vyomi's wire layer never verifies an HMAC-signed request against the issued secret — the separate S3-compatible XML endpoint these keys authenticate against is not implemented.

features.t: Turbo replication (dual-region RPO ASYNC_TURBO)
x: The rpo setting is validated (dual-region buckets only) and every change is recorded as a bucket operation; Vyomi keeps a single copy, so the 15-minute replication guarantee is not measured.

features.t: Autoclass (automatic storage-class transitions)
x: Transitions run for real on each object's access clock (STANDARD to NEARLINE after 30 idle days; to COLDLINE at 90 and ARCHIVE at 365 with an ARCHIVE terminal class; a read returns the object to STANDARD) and are evaluated when the bucket's objects are listed or read, not by a background job. Storage classes do not change pricing or retrieval latency in Vyomi.

features.t: Per-object customer-supplied encryption keys (CSEK)
x: The x-goog-encryption-* headers are validated; only the key's SHA-256 is stored, bytes at rest are encrypted with a SHA-256 counter-mode keystream derived from the key (not AES), reads need the same key, and compose/copy of such objects is not supported.
